goal: Establish whether agy 1.1.2 accepts direct injection of a saved consumer refresh credential in Linux SSH file-fallback mode.
completed: A copied expired token record authenticated in a fresh isolated home without browser login.
A minimal record with an invalid expired access token and valid refresh token refreshed and authenticated successfully.
Both isolated test homes and all sensitive copies were removed; default state was not modified.
nextActions: Implement a version-gated credential-envelope module and synthetic tests, then validate two independently enrolled accounts before enabling real profile commands.
decisions: Direct refresh-token injection is a viable agy 1.1.2 Linux SSH profile mechanism; the official client continues to own refresh and backend requests.
openQuestions: Does Google rotate the refresh token during long-lived use, and can agy-auth capture that update atomically per profile?
What at-rest protection should project-owned refresh credentials use?

notRun: Second independently enrolled account, concurrent switching, rollback, and upgrade behavior were not run.

risks: The contract is reverse engineered and version-specific; refresh credentials are bearer secrets and require protected storage.
doNotRepeat: Do not copy live access tokens; the minimal refresh-token envelope is sufficient.
Do not enable production switching from single-account evidence.
